title: Confusables (B1)
note: English pairs that Czech collapses into one verb: lend/borrow (půjčit), bring/take, remember/remind, look/watch/see, hear/listen. The direction of the action is the whole point. First draft 2026-09-02. · 2026-09-04 B1 loop: **learn was tiled twice** — *learn (get)* against teach in block 1 and *learn (the result)* against study in block 3, so one word had two tiles and two Czech glosses. Block 3 now pairs **study / practise**. · C52, which the draft's own note flagged as the doubt: each block gains a **contrast table page** — every pair side by side with the direction spelled out (*lend = you give it* / *borrow = you take it*), sitting right after that block's picture board. Eighteen separate pages, one per pair, would be unplayable; three tables put the same contrast on screen. · sentences 8 → 36, one gappable frame per lemma. Three of the eight shipped frames used a past form (*borrowed*, *watched*, *heard*) and produced no gap. E10: Use is use_mode rewrite, 12 items, and on this pack the paraphrase is the trap itself: *take* → borrow, *give me* → lend, *see* → watch, *hear* → listen to, *home* → house. · Pool-checked against everything taught before leaf_confusables_b1 — 0 unknown types. · 2026-09-04: five rewrite items re-cut so replacing the underline reconstructs the answer. · 2026-09-05 B1 loop: sentence texture. 20 of 36 Use sentences were FLAT or THIN under check_sentence_texture.py. A confusable pair is taught by a minimal sentence, which is the shape the check catches. All 20 rewritten to make one clause move and carry two or more already-taught words, while keeping each sentence a context where only one of the pair fits — that is the whole point of the leaf, so no rewrite was allowed to make the cousin acceptable too. 0/36 fail now. `bridge` was drafted onto the see item and is untaught before slot 53.

rows: **lend** = you give it · *I lent him my car.*
**borrow** = you take it · *I borrowed his car.*
**remind** = you make somebody think of it
**watch** = it moves and you follow it

intro.title: You will use these words in
intro.note: Czech has one verb where English has two. *Půjčit* is **lend** and **borrow**; *učit* is **teach** and **learn**; *říct* is **say** and **tell**. The direction of the action decides which one.
intro.note_cz: Čeština má jedno sloveso tam, kde angličtina má dvě. Rozhoduje směr děje.
